name: setlist
description: setlist.fm is a crowd-sourced database of concert setlists. This CLI wraps the official setlist.fm REST API 1.0 (api.setlist.fm) to search and look up artists, setlists, venues, cities, countries and users.
notes: An AWS WAF bot challenge blocks www.setlist.fm, so no website requests could be recorded. All commands use the official REST API at https://api.setlist.fm/rest/1.0/, built from the Swagger spec (E2). None of them were replayed during exploration.

Every API call needs an API key in the x-api-key header. Pass it with --api_key. Get a key for free at https://www.setlist.fm/settings/api (this needs a setlist.fm account). Without a key, requests return 403. The key is optional in the spec only because no shared key can be hard-coded.
The Accept: application/json header is sent so responses come back as JSON instead of XML.
List responses have the shape {type, itemsPerPage (20), page, total, <items>}. Use --p to page and compare page*itemsPerPage with total to know when to stop.
Setlist dates (eventDate, the date filter) use dd-MM-yyyy. lastUpdated uses yyyyMMddHHmmss.

Typical flow: search-artists, then take mbid into list-artist-setlists or search-setlists --artistMbid, then take id into get-setlist. The songs are in sets.set[].song[].name. Encores have sets.set[].encore set.
The API is rate-limited (about 2 requests per second and a daily quota per key) and is free for non-commercial use only.
The example IDs (setlist 63de4613, version 7be1aaa0, venue 6bd6ca6e, city 5357527, user Adam-Adam) come from the API documentation and setlist.fm conventions, not from recorded responses.
